audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows said Rumble while their own whys say Jax or even: whys[1] 'Counter Strike flips any auto exchange', whys[2] 'the stun locks the dashless Rumble out of his own channel', whys[4] 'your cleanest kill window', whys[5] 'your item timing owns this window', whys[6] 'the overall lane stays even'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill / Jax / Jax / Skill / Jax / Jax / Skill at a 50.83% win rate. Rumble has no dash and Scrap Shield is only a 6s speed burst, so every stage where Jax can reach him belongs to Jax; the even stages are the ones where Electro Harpoon's slow keeps him out of range.
audit.corrected: phases[1]/win[1], phases[2]/win[2], phases[4]/win[4], phases[5]/win[5] to Jax and phases[6]/win[6] to Skill — matched pairs with ratings realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys were generic; the Levels 4-5 and Level 6 rows in particular said nothing about what actually changes.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a flat 6s — much shorter than the page's 'bait it, then commit' framing implies, which is exactly why levels 4-5 stay even rather than becoming a Jax window. Flamespitter is 10/9/8/7/6s, The Equalizer 130/105/80s against Grandmaster's Might at 110s.
audit.corrected: Phase whys rebuilt on Scrap Shield's 6s, Flamespitter's 10s and the two ultimate cooldowns.

audit.why: This page's interaction work is already right and matches the mirror: Flamespitter is a sustained magic tick, not a basic attack, so Counter Strike does not make it whiff — the dodge is for his autos and the recast stun is what interrupts him. whys[0] and early both state this correctly, and Rumble having no dash is the reason the stun sticks.
audit.corrected: No change needed; restated from Jax's side in the Level 3 phase why so the chart rows carry the same fact.

audit.whatIsWrong: Scrap Shield is named the matchup-defining cooldown across breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5] and report[9] — with no number. It is 6 seconds.
audit.why: A 6s shield is not a window you plan an all-in around; the real punishable cooldowns are Flamespitter (10s at rank 1) and Heat/Overheat lockout, during which he cannot cast at all.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the phase whys; the overheat lockout named as the actual commit window.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Rumble's Scrap Shield is down.
edits.after: Counter Strike flips any auto exchange, and the recast stun interrupts Flamespitter (10s at rank 1) outright.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Rumble must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Leap Strike in while he is casting: E dodges his autos, not the flame cone, but the stun ends the channel and he has no dash.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Scrap Shield's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even: Electro Harpoon's slow and Scrap Shield's 6s speed burst kite you between trades, so go when his Heat locks him out of casting.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Rumble's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might (110s) tanks his magic tick and cycles faster than The Equalizer (130s) — force the all-in off his R's line.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Scrap Shield's cooldown.
edits.after: Trinity Force's Spellblade and move speed carry you through the harpoon slow — this is the item window where you stick to him.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Rumble carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: You own the side-lane 1v1, but The Equalizer decides fights you are not in — the late game turns on map control, not the duel.

notes: IMPORTANT — the mirror is wrong and I did not follow it. audits/top/rumble__jax.json records: "'Grandmaster's Might' is a fabricated/legacy name; Riot's is Grandmaster-at-Arms." That is backwards. Grandmaster's Might is Jax's R; 'Grandmaster at Arms' is his champion TITLE, which is precisely why the wrong name keeps appearing across this champion's pages. This jax__rumble page already uses Grandmaster's Might correctly in five fields, so I changed nothing there — but if that mirror note is acted on it will rename a correct ability to the title across the Rumble page and possibly others. Recommend a human confirm against champ-data/_kits/jax.json before any rename runs. Separately, this page's Counter Strike / Flamespitter interaction is correct as written. Data note: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json lists Electro Harpoon's cooldown as 0.5s, which is the between-harpoon recharge, not the ability cooldown — I wrote no number for it.
